lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice A: theorems about parallelograms

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

steps: Both are supplementary to the same angle.
Angles supplementary to the same angle are equal.
workedSolution.answer: both supplementary to a common angle

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 69°. Find the measure of the corresponding angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 47° and 53°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 104°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 34. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 68, and it is parallel to the third side
17, and it is parallel to the third side
17, and it is perpendicular to the third side
34, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: Vertical angles are congruent by definition.
The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.
The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 131°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 59° and 52°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 90°. Find the opposite angle.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 24. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 12, and it is perpendicular to the third side
12, and it is parallel to the third side
48, and it is parallel to the third side
24, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: Every quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other.
The diagonals are congruent, so they must bisect each other.
Alternate interior angles give two pairs of congruent angles, and the opposite sides are congruent, so the triangles formed are congruent by ASA.
The diagonals are perpendicular, which forces bisection.
